selected.pre_reveal_mechanism_hypothesis: distribute() is permissionless and pays royaltyfee + rounding dust to _msgSender() (an arbitrary caller), not to the protocol/owner. The royalty rate is owner-set (updateRoyalty onlyOwner) but the proceeds are captured by whoever calls distribute -> value misallocation / MEV skim of the curator reward pool.
selected.falsifier: If sending royalty+dust to msg.sender is the intended keeper incentive (no other keeper reward exists) and the protocol does not expect the royalty to accrue to owner/treasury, this is benign-by-design.

selected.pre_reveal_mechanism_hypothesis: distribute() splits rewards by SPOT curator share (getShareNumber at call time). An attacker buys a large share of a credId that has accumulated rewards, then calls the permissionless distribute() in the same tx to capture distributeAmount*share/totalNum, diluting curators who curated earlier. SHARE_LOCK_PERIOD (10m) blocks same-block resale but not buy->distribute; attacker holds the position through the lock and exits, profiting if accumulated rewards exceed bonding-curve round-trip cost.
selected.falsifier: If accumulated rewards can never exceed the marginal bonding-curve cost + fees of acquiring enough share within the lock window, the attack is unprofitable -> benign.

selected.pre_reveal_mechanism_hypothesis: EXPECTED BENIGN: gasless withdraw is EIP-712 signed over (from,to,amount,nonce,deadline), nonce-incremented (replay-safe), deadline-checked, amount<=balance. No obvious flaw -> included as a negative control to test that the gate/PoC layer correctly does NOT manufacture a finding.
selected.falsifier: A reproducible signature replay / wrong-account withdraw / balance underflow would refute the benign expectation.
